transcript: Joy is a new musical based on the life of Joy Mangano, inventor and entrepreneur from Long Island who is most well-known for inventing the Miracle Mop. Over two acts that I think could have been one, we learn how this invention came to be and how Joy went from a struggling single mom to a mogul and QVC icon. It's a simple story in that it focuses on one character and her dreams, and from the get go, this musical does a great job of establishing her as an underdog. Betsy Wolfe as Joy has an extremely likeable presence, so it's easy to root for her. I also appreciated how the time and place in the 90s is well-established here, though the energy pulsing throughout the production falls somewhere on that line between quirky and cringe. I enjoyed the music — I found it pleasant, even if not very memorable, and I enjoyed the way it was performed by the entire cast. Unfortunately, Act 2 lost a lot of steam for me and the buoyancy of the production faltered, but otherwise I thought this production was solid. It's the kind of material that really benefits from someone like Betsy Wolfe in the lead role who can ground it and bring depth to a relatively surface-level plot. Overall, I didn't find this life-changing, but I was pleasantly surprised. If this interests you, it is running through August 17th. With that, another playbill for my collection.
